headline: Town boards finalized recommendations and warrant articles for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, including water connections, trail funding, and zoning.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, town boards completed their preparations for key warrant articles. The Advisory Committee voted to recommend spending $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the Parkerville Road landfill to town water, while the Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to send the Peninsula Trail bridge funding request to voters without removing contingency funds. The Select Board announced over $1.3 million in grant awards, including $1.1 million for a water main replacement on Southville Road, and declined a request to retain $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority for Breakneck Hill. Regional school subcommittees reviewed $460,000 in high school capital requests and noted an expected $800,000 drop in regional debt service in FY28.

highlights.title: Water connection recommendation for homes near landfill
highlights.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7, which uses $240,000 from water retained earnings to fully fund municipal water connections for two homes affected by the Parkerville Road landfill.

highlights.title: $1.1 million MassWorks grant for Southville Road water main
highlights.why: The town announced the receipt of a $1.1 million state grant to replace 1,300 feet of water main on Southville Road with 12-inch ductile iron pipe.

highlights.title: Advancement of Peninsula Trail CPA funding request
highlights.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance the Article 4 funding request for the Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge as printed, deciding against floor amendments to remove project contingency.

highlights.title: FY28 Algonquin capital projects and debt reduction
highlights.why: School officials reviewed $460,000 across five proposed high school capital projects and highlighted an estimated $800,000 net drop in regional debt service in FY28 as 2004 renovation debt retires.
highlights.body: Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee Operational Budget and Capital Planning Subcommittees

highlights.title: Refusal to alter Breakneck Hill debt rescission
highlights.why: The Select Board unanimously declined to support a floor amendment holding back $100,000 in unissued borrowing authority, opting to rescind the full $727,960 in remaining debt under Article 6.

highlights.title: Support for two-family dwelling warrant article
highlights.why: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted unanimously to move forward with the two-family dwelling warrant article as drafted rather than introducing last-minute wording changes regarding lot sizes.
